answer: An agent economy can limit Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can earn reputation or claim rewards. The protocol caps how quickly new identities gain influence, then penalizes proven double-claims or coordinated fraud by confiscating their stake. An attacker can still create many accounts, but each must tie up real capital, and detected fraud destroys it; splitting funds among identities does not multiply voting weight. Opal, willow, and ocean can be agent names, but none grants an exception.
